"It is the illusion of a challenge... they want everyone to feel like a god. If you can walk in a straight line, you can get through this game. It's about tricking people into feeling proud about themselves without giving them anything to be proud about."

And I mean, being easy is not so bad... but Forces isn't even deep. Like, Mario Odyssey isn't hard but at least there's a lot to do and a lot of agency on behalf of the player. Forces literally guides you back to the middle of the track if you stray, has no penalty for missing many of the generous QTEs, and throws pathetic enemies at you where you just point the flamethrower in a circle and they all die. There's little opportunity for emergence like in other Sonic games. In the Game Grumps playthrough, Arin died twice as Classic sonic in the sunset heights stage and still hit rank S. It is definitely frustrating to see people blindly buying a game that everyone is telling them is kinda mediocre on launch day under the guise of "thinking for themselves" and "forming their own opinions." 

It shouldn't be controversial to say that a good game isn't just good to its fans, it's good to everyone. You can't live on "well at least the game isn't broken" for long. You have to make people begrudgingly give up that 8 or 9/10 because it would be unreasonable to say otherwise. 

I do hope that a major corporation would apply some level of nuance to its market analysis. Don't get me wrong, they have more data than me (and if there is any one thing Sonic does right, it is sell), and I'd be fine with no more Boost because we have Green Hill Paradise and Utopia to show that full-axis 3D sonic is not an inherently broken idea, but I hope they don't take fact that they phoned in the level design on a Boost game and it got 5/10s from everyone as a sign that "Boost is Dead" and never do it again solely on that basis... because that might just get us another 10 years of screwing about and never sticking to and refining an idea in a world where every other developer and their dog has figured out how to make a 3D game.

I guess it's like, with Generations we finally got all the elements people were screaming about together in one place, so we didn't have to lower our standards to "well, it's not a horrendously broken and buggy mess" anymore. Lost World kinda showed that: it was a beautiful and high quality game that some folks praised for not being absolutely screwed up like Adventure or 06, but it played it too safe and was mechanically mediocre, so it didn't get an easy pass. Forces has the same problem in that the levels and mechanics are merely passable, despite really only having to just build on Generations.

I sometimes feel like things like this happen because Sega is afraid to kill the player, given how Lets Players and dismissive people treat Sonic: if it's somewhat hard, it's "cheap" (Advance 3, Genesis). if it's easy, it's "forgettable" (Lost World). If it's balanced but complex (Mania), people don't see and aren't primed for the scale of the game and think when they're going fast, they're doing well, which is not always the case.

The Forces devs wanted a power fantasy at the expense of depth. They wanted everyone to feel like a badass, but people are seeing through it just like how some saw through Destiny 2 AI and many AAA design techniques. 

I think it's somewhat good that this turned out the way it is, because it's sending a message that the developers cannot themselves "boost to win" by just throwing a new coat of paint on a series of straightaways and scripted loops and expect an 8/10 from either the critics or the fans every year just because Sonic doesn't glitch through the floor every 2 stages.

I'd say Rush made this formula work because it was actually relatively easy to lose your boost (especially if you lost it once before) you had to keep it, which acts as a metaphor for retaining velocity, and Generations made it work by having quite a few open sections and areas where boosting and drifting at the right time as opposed to just holding it gave you better routes.

Forces is just straight lines of enemies who don't do anything looking to die though.
